etymology: From Latin impossibilis, from in- meaning “not” and possibilis meaning “able to be done.” In Scripture the word marks the boundary between creaturely inability and the living God for whom no word shall fail.
biblical_def: Impossible names what cannot be done by creaturely strength, natural power, fallen will, or human wisdom. Scripture uses the word to humble man and exalt God. With men salvation is impossible, for no rich man can buy his way through the needle's eye, no sinner can quicken his own dead heart, and no flesh shall glory in His presence; but with God all things are possible. The impossible birth of Isaac, the virgin conception of Christ, the new birth of a sinner, the resurrection of the dead, and the final perseverance of the saints all declare the same doctrine: God is not limited by the weakness, age, barrenness, deadness, poverty, fear, or opposition of man. Yet Scripture also says there are things impossible in another sense: it is impossible for God to lie, impossible for His promise to fail, and impossible to please Him without faith. Thus the word guards two truths at once. Man cannot save himself; God cannot deny Himself. The Christian therefore does not use impossible as the final word over God's promise, but as the confession that the work must be of grace, by power, and unto the glory of God alone.
webster_summary: Not able to be done by creaturely power; in Scripture, the boundary where man's inability is exposed and God's power, truth, and grace are displayed.
webster_full: IMPOSSIBLE, not possible; that cannot be done, effected, or accomplished.
That which exceeds created power or natural means.
That which cannot be true because it contradicts the nature, promise, or decree of God.
In Scripture, the word often sets man's inability beside God's omnipotence.
It also names what God cannot do because He cannot lie, deny Himself, or cease to be holy.
scriptures: But Jesus beheld them, and said unto them, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
For with God nothing shall be impossible.
That by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to lie, we might have a strong consolation.
But without faith it is impossible to please him: for he that cometh to God must believe that he is.
corruption_summary: Modern unbelief often treats impossible as a verdict over God's promise, while modern presumption treats nothing as impossible to man's will; Scripture corrects both errors.
corruption_paragraphs: The unbelieving corruption of this word uses impossible as a wall against the promise of God. It looks at age, barrenness, money, statistics, politics, disease, weakness, or death and concludes that the LORD's word cannot stand. That was Sarah's laughter apart from grace, Israel's fear before giants, and the disciples' astonishment when Jesus said the rich could scarcely enter the kingdom. Scripture does not teach men to deny difficulty; it teaches them to deny that difficulty is sovereign. The impossible is no obstacle to Him who calleth those things which be not as though they were.

The opposite corruption is man-centered presumption: motivational religion says nothing is impossible if a man believes in himself, manifests his future, or summons enough positive energy. Scripture says no such thing. With man, salvation is impossible; without faith, pleasing God is impossible; apart from Christ, we can do nothing. The Christian hope is not human potential but divine power. Impossible therefore becomes a worship word: it humbles the sinner, steadies faith, and magnifies the God whose promise cannot lie and whose arm is not shortened that it cannot save.
roots_summary: Impossible joins the negative prefix to the word possible; biblically it marks the limit of man and the certainty of God's power and truth.
roots_lines: English — impossible, that which cannot be accomplished by created power.
Doctrine — man's inability is real; God's omnipotence is greater.
Boundary — impossible for man does not mean impossible for God.
usage: The disciples learned that salvation is impossible with men but possible with God.
The virgin birth declares that with God nothing shall be impossible.
Because it is impossible for God to lie, His promise gives strong consolation to His people.
